Name: Hydrogen
Name Origin: From Greek hydro (water) + genes (forming): "water-former," because burning it produces water.

Name: Helium
Name Origin: From Greek helios, the Sun, where it was detected as a spectral line in 1868, before it was found on Earth.

Name: Lithium
Name Origin: From Greek lithos, stone, because it was found in a mineral, unlike sodium and potassium, which were known from plant ashes.

Name: Beryllium
Name Origin: Named after the mineral beryl (Greek beryllos), in which it was found.

Name: Boron
Name Origin: From borax (via Arabic buraq and Persian burah), the mineral it was isolated from, with the "-on" ending of carbon, which it resembles.

Name: Carbon
Name Origin: From Latin carbo, charcoal.

Name: Nitrogen
Name Origin: From Greek nitron (saltpetre) + genes (forming), because it is a component of saltpetre. In French it is still called azote, "lifeless."

Name: Oxygen
Name Origin: From Greek oxys (sharp, acid) + genes (forming): "acid-former," from the mistaken belief that all acids contain oxygen.

Name: Fluorine
Name Origin: Named after the mineral fluorite, from Latin fluere, to flow, because the mineral was used as a flux to help ores melt.

Name: Neon
Name Origin: From Greek neos, new.

Name: Sodium
Name Origin: From soda (sodium hydroxide), from which it was first isolated. The symbol Na comes from Latin natrium, from natron, a natural sodium salt.

Name: Magnesium
Name Origin: Named after Magnesia, a district of Greece that was a source of magnesia minerals.

Name: Aluminium
Name Origin: From Latin alumen, alum, a salt used since antiquity as a dye fixative.

Name: Silicon
Name Origin: From Latin silex (silicis), flint, with the "-on" ending of boron and carbon.

Name: Phosphorus
Name Origin: From Greek phosphoros, "light-bearer," because its white form glows in the dark.

Name: Sulfur
Name Origin: From Latin sulfur, a word of uncertain origin.

Name: Chlorine
Name Origin: From Greek chloros, pale green or yellow-green, the colour of the gas.

Name: Argon
Name Origin: From Greek argos, idle or lazy, because it is so chemically inert.

Name: Potassium
Name Origin: From potash ("pot ash," plant ashes leached in pots), from which it was first isolated. The symbol K comes from Latin kalium, from Arabic al-qali, plant ashes, also the source of "alkali."

Name: Calcium
Name Origin: From Latin calx (calcis), lime.

Name: Scandium
Name Origin: From Latin Scandia, Scandinavia, where it was found.

Name: Titanium
Name Origin: Named after the Titans of Greek mythology, by analogy with uranium (named after the planet Uranus).

Name: Vanadium
Name Origin: Named after Vanadís, an Old Norse name for the goddess Freyja, because its compounds come in many beautiful colours.

Name: Chromium
Name Origin: From Greek chroma, colour, because its compounds are so vividly coloured.

Name: Manganese
Name Origin: From the black mineral "magnesia nigra"; "manganese" is a corrupted form of magnesia, used to tell it apart from magnesium.

Name: Iron
Name Origin: From Old English īsern/īren. The symbol Fe comes from Latin ferrum.

Name: Cobalt
Name Origin: From German Kobold, a goblin, which miners blamed for ores that looked valuable but yielded no metal.

Name: Nickel
Name Origin: From German Kupfernickel, "copper-demon," an ore that looked like copper ore but yielded no copper.

Name: Copper
Name Origin: From Latin cuprum, from Cyprium aes, "metal of Cyprus," a major ancient copper source. The symbol Cu comes from the same word.

Name: Zinc
Name Origin: From German Zink, probably from Zinke, a prong or spike, describing its jagged crystals.

Name: Gallium
Name Origin: From Latin Gallia, France.

Name: Germanium
Name Origin: From Latin Germania, Germany, the discoverer's homeland.

Name: Arsenic
Name Origin: From Greek arsenikon, the yellow pigment orpiment, borrowed from Persian zarnikh, golden.

Name: Selenium
Name Origin: From Greek selene, the Moon, because it resembles tellurium, which was named after the Earth.

Name: Bromine
Name Origin: From Greek bromos, stench, because of its strong, unpleasant smell.

Name: Krypton
Name Origin: From Greek kryptos, hidden, because it was found hiding in the residue of evaporated liquid air.

Name: Rubidium
Name Origin: From Latin rubidus, deep red, after the red lines in its spectrum.

Name: Strontium
Name Origin: Named after Strontian, a village in Scotland whose mines produced the mineral strontianite.

Name: Yttrium
Name Origin: Named after Ytterby, a village in Sweden whose quarry gave its name to four elements: yttrium, terbium, erbium, and ytterbium.

Name: Zirconium
Name Origin: Named after the mineral zircon, from Persian zargun, gold-coloured.

Name: Niobium
Name Origin: Named after Niobe, daughter of Tantalus in Greek mythology, because niobium is almost chemically identical to tantalum.

Name: Molybdenum
Name Origin: From Greek molybdos, lead, because its ore was confused with lead ore.

Name: Technetium
Name Origin: From Greek technetos, artificial: it was the first element made artificially.

Name: Ruthenium
Name Origin: From Latin Ruthenia, Russia, where it was discovered.

Name: Rhodium
Name Origin: From Greek rhodon, rose, because of the rose-red colour of its salts.

Name: Palladium
Name Origin: Named after the asteroid Pallas, discovered a year earlier and itself named after the goddess Pallas Athena.

Name: Silver
Name Origin: From Old English seolfor. The symbol Ag comes from Latin argentum, from a root meaning bright or white.

Name: Cadmium
Name Origin: From Latin cadmia, the ancient name for calamine (zinc ore), after Cadmus, the legendary founder of Thebes.

Name: Indium
Name Origin: Named after the indigo blue line in its spectrum.

Name: Tin
Name Origin: From Old English tin. The symbol Sn comes from Latin stannum.

Name: Antimony
Name Origin: From medieval Latin antimonium, of obscure origin. The symbol Sb comes from Latin stibium, its mineral stibnite.

Name: Tellurium
Name Origin: From Latin tellus, earth.

Name: Iodine
Name Origin: From Greek iodes, violet, after the colour of its vapour.

Name: Xenon
Name Origin: From Greek xenos, stranger or foreigner.

Name: Cesium
Name Origin: From Latin caesius, sky blue, after the blue lines in its spectrum.

Name: Barium
Name Origin: From Greek barys, heavy, after the unusually dense mineral baryte.

Name: Lanthanum
Name Origin: From Greek lanthanein, to lie hidden, because it was found hiding in cerium oxide.

Name: Cerium
Name Origin: Named after Ceres, the first asteroid discovered, itself named after the Roman goddess of agriculture.

Name: Praseodymium
Name Origin: From Greek prasios didymos, "green twin," for its green salts; it was split from didymium ("twin").

Name: Neodymium
Name Origin: From Greek neos didymos, "new twin," the other half of didymium (with praseodymium).

Name: Promethium
Name Origin: Named after Prometheus, the Titan who stole fire from the gods, alluding to the promise and danger of nuclear power.

Name: Samarium
Name Origin: Named after the mineral samarskite, which honours the Russian mining engineer Samarsky-Bykhovets.

Name: Europium
Name Origin: Named after Europe.

Name: Gadolinium
Name Origin: Named after the mineral gadolinite, which honours Johan Gadolin, a Finnish rare-earth chemist.

Name: Terbium
Name Origin: Named after Ytterby, the Swedish village whose quarry gave its name to four elements.

Name: Dysprosium
Name Origin: From Greek dysprositos, "hard to get at," because it was so difficult to separate.

Name: Holmium
Name Origin: From Latin Holmia, Stockholm.

Name: Erbium
Name Origin: Named after Ytterby, the Swedish village whose quarry gave its name to four elements.

Name: Thulium
Name Origin: Named after Thule, the mythical far-northern land, often associated with Scandinavia.

Name: Ytterbium
Name Origin: Named after Ytterby, the Swedish village whose quarry gave its name to four elements.

Name: Lutetium
Name Origin: From Lutetia, the Latin name for Paris, where it was discovered.

Name: Hafnium
Name Origin: From Hafnia, the Latin name for Copenhagen, where it was discovered.

Name: Tantalum
Name Origin: Named after Tantalus, who in Greek myth stood in water he could never drink, because its oxide cannot "drink" acid.

Name: Tungsten
Name Origin: From Swedish tung sten, "heavy stone." The symbol W comes from wolfram, from the mineral wolframite.

Name: Rhenium
Name Origin: From Latin Rhenus, the Rhine.

Name: Osmium
Name Origin: From Greek osme, smell, after the pungent odour of its oxide.

Name: Iridium
Name Origin: From Greek iris, rainbow, because its salts come in so many colours.

Name: Platinum
Name Origin: From Spanish platina, "little silver."

Name: Gold
Name Origin: From Old English gold, related to "yellow." The symbol Au comes from Latin aurum.

Name: Mercury
Name Origin: Named after the planet and swift messenger god Mercury, suiting this quick, mobile liquid metal. The symbol Hg comes from Greek hydrargyros, "water-silver."

Name: Thallium
Name Origin: From Greek thallos, a green shoot, after the bright green line in its spectrum.

Name: Lead
Name Origin: From Old English lead. The symbol Pb comes from Latin plumbum, which also gave us "plumbing."

Name: Bismuth
Name Origin: From German Wismut, of uncertain origin.

Name: Polonium
Name Origin: Named after Poland, Marie Curie's homeland, then partitioned between other powers.

Name: Astatine
Name Origin: From Greek astatos, unstable, because all its isotopes are short-lived.

Name: Radon
Name Origin: Named after radium, which gives it off, with the "-on" ending of the noble gases.

Name: Francium
Name Origin: Named after France, where it was discovered.

Name: Radium
Name Origin: From Latin radius, ray, because of its intense radioactivity.

Name: Actinium
Name Origin: From Greek aktis (aktinos), ray or beam, because of its radioactivity.

Name: Thorium
Name Origin: Named after Thor, the Norse god of thunder.

Name: Protactinium
Name Origin: From Greek protos, first, + actinium: "parent of actinium," because it decays into actinium.

Name: Uranium
Name Origin: Named after the planet Uranus, which had been discovered just eight years earlier.

Name: Neptunium
Name Origin: Named after Neptune, the planet beyond Uranus, because it comes right after uranium.

Name: Plutonium
Name Origin: Named after Pluto, then considered the next planet after Neptune.

Name: Americium
Name Origin: Named after the Americas, by analogy with europium directly above it.

Name: Curium
Name Origin: Named after Marie and Pierre Curie, by analogy with gadolinium (named after a chemist) directly above it.

Name: Berkelium
Name Origin: Named after Berkeley, California, where it was made, by analogy with terbium (named after a village) directly above it.

Name: Californium
Name Origin: Named after California and the University of California, where it was made.

Name: Einsteinium
Name Origin: Named after Albert Einstein.

Name: Fermium
Name Origin: Named after Enrico Fermi, builder of the first nuclear reactor.

Name: Mendelevium
Name Origin: Named after Dmitri Mendeleev, creator of the periodic table.

Name: Nobelium
Name Origin: Named after Alfred Nobel.

Name: Lawrencium
Name Origin: Named after Ernest Lawrence, inventor of the cyclotron.

Name: Rutherfordium
Name Origin: Named after Ernest Rutherford, the father of nuclear physics.

Name: Dubnium
Name Origin: Named after Dubna, Russia, home of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research.

Name: Seaborgium
Name Origin: Named after Glenn Seaborg, who discovered or co-discovered ten elements. It was the first element named after a living person.

Name: Bohrium
Name Origin: Named after Niels Bohr, whose model of the atom underpins atomic structure.

Name: Hassium
Name Origin: From Latin Hassia, the German state of Hesse, where it was made.

Name: Meitnerium
Name Origin: Named after Lise Meitner, co-discoverer of nuclear fission.

Name: Darmstadtium
Name Origin: Named after Darmstadt, the German city where it was made.

Name: Roentgenium
Name Origin: Named after Wilhelm Röntgen, the discoverer of X-rays.

Name: Copernicium
Name Origin: Named after Nicolaus Copernicus, who proposed that the Earth orbits the Sun.

Name: Nihonium
Name Origin: From Nihon, a Japanese name for Japan. It was the first element discovered in Asia.

Name: Flerovium
Name Origin: Named after the Flerov Laboratory at Dubna, itself named after the physicist Georgy Flyorov.

Name: Moscovium
Name Origin: Named after Moscow Oblast, the region where Dubna is located.

Name: Livermorium
Name Origin: Named after Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California, which helped make it.

Name: Tennessine
Name Origin: Named after Tennessee, home of Oak Ridge National Laboratory, which helped make it. It ends in "-ine" like the other halogens.

Name: Oganesson
Name Origin: Named after Yuri Oganessian, a Russian physicist who led superheavy-element research. Its "-on" ending matches the other noble gases.
